Chain-linking is accomplished for each of the three
subperiods by rescaling; this moves the year in which
current and constant price versions of the same time
series have the same value, without altering the trend
of either. Components of gross domestic product
(GDP) are individually rescaled and summed to pro-
vide GDP and its subaggregates. In this process a
rescaling deviation may occur between the constant
price GDP by industrial origin and the constant price
GDP by expenditure. Such rescaling deviations are
absorbed under the heading private consumption, etc.
on the assumption that GDP by industrial origin is a
more reliable estimate than GDP by expenditure.
